source.citation: [A survey of the residences of Prairie Avenue, Sixteenth to Twenty-second Street, west side then east side, beginning 'Chicago has every reason to be proud of her beautiful homes.'] The Daily Inter Ocean (Chicago), 2 January 1887; transcribed on chicagology.com, Prairie Avenue page, under the heading 'Inter Ocean, January 2, 1887'.
what_it_does_not_supply: the issue's page or column, or a reading of the printed text: only the transcription was read
any planting beyond a lawn and a conservatory: no tree, bed or garden is named
what_it_supplies: Allerton's lawn south of his house, valued at $117,000 in 1887
the Field conservatory on the south side in 1887
the Glessner grounds enclosed and hidden from the street, the house and stable joined
Einstein's 1628 set back in 'well-kept grounds'; Shortall's grounds behind an iron fence
the Dexter and Pullman grounds adjoining with no marked line between them
unimproved lots on the east side south of Eighteenth Street in winter 1886-87
